summary: A 35-foot stone tower on Mattapoisett Harbor, lit in 1838; its keepers, the 1923 automation, a 1937 sale with a one-cent bid, and a Friends group that gives tours.

structures.note: 35 ft (10.7 m) as built (NRHP; LighthouseFriends); 39 ft (12 m) to the centre of the lantern today (USLHS). USLHS gives 1838 as the tower year.
NRHP 1981 describes a stone oil house of 1837; LighthouseFriends says a brick oil house was constructed in 1907
Original keeper's dwelling; demolished in 1888 after a hurricane (LighthouseFriends)
Frame house erected on the old foundation; moved off the site to Wing's Neck (1920, 1923 or 1930; sources differ)

access.note: The grounds are a town park open to the public. The tower is open on scheduled tours run by the Friends of Ned's Point Lighthouse in summer (2026 season: 20 June to 1 October, weather permitting).

facts.agency: U.S. Coast Guard (the light); Town of Mattapoisett (the grounds); Friends of Ned's Point Lighthouse (tours)

events.note: Stone tower, lantern and keeper's dwelling built for about $4,500 (NRHP) or the $5,000 Congress approved (LighthouseFriends)
Four-acre site bought from H.H. Edwards through his guardian Barnabus Hiller for $240
Lamps lit 21 March 1838 (NRHP); activated in March 1838 (LighthouseFriends). USLHS gives 1837 as year established
Lieutenant Edward Carpender's inspection finds the tower and dwelling leak and the lantern too low (as quoted by LighthouseFriends)
Fifth-order Fresnel lens installed (LighthouseFriends); USLHS gives 1888 as the year the original lens was installed
Sea wall destroyed (NRHP chronology)
Hurricane nearly destroys the station; original stone dwelling demolished and a frame house erected (LighthouseFriends)
Frame keeper's dwelling replaces the stone one (LighthouseFriends)
Present lantern room installed (LighthouseFriends)
Brick oil house constructed (LighthouseFriends)
Light fully automated; USLHS and LighthouseFriends both give 1923
Lighthouse Service Bulletin lists a change in illuminant at Ned Point (acetylene is mentioned in the 1923 entry; the scan text is garbled)
Keeper's dwelling floated across Buzzards Bay to Wing's Neck, Bourne (NRHP chronology gives 1920, NRHP site description 1930; LighthouseFriends 1923)
Government puts the light property up for sale 'to the lowest bidder' after a clerical change; sixteen bids, all rejected (as cited by LighthouseFriends)
Coast Guard decommissions the light (LighthouseFriends); USLHS: discontinued 1952-1961
Grounds, except the tower and right of way, sold to the Town of Mattapoisett for a public park
Reactivated with a new modern lens: six-second isophase
Local Coast Guard Auxiliary Flotilla adopts the light; tower renovated 1995-96
Closed to the public because of lead paint contamination
Friends of Ned's Point Lighthouse formed by Coast Guard Auxiliary members to raise restoration funds
Reopened to the public after the lead paint was removed

corrections.proposed: tower, stone, built 1837, 10.7 m (35 ft) as built; 12 m to lantern centre today
corrections.why: The NRHP chronology dates the 35-foot stone tower to 1837 (lamps lit March 1838). The 12.0 m in the record matches the 39 ft height to the lantern centre in USLHS, not the tower as built.
The NRHP chronology gives 3/21/1838 for the lamps lit; LighthouseFriends says the light was activated in March 1838. 1837 is when the station was established and the tower built.
LighthouseFriends says the Coast Guard decommissioned the light in 1952. The 1951 date has no source read here.

resolved_conflicts.field: still lit (record: sources differ on whether the light is still lit)
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's question was whether the light is still shown. It was discontinued in 1952, reactivated in 1961 with a six-second isophase lens, and the USLHS lists it as an active aid to navigation. The Friends scheduled tours on the tower for summer 2026.

notes_for_editor: 1) Start of service: the NRHP chronology has the tower built in 1837 and the lamps lit on 21 March 1838; USLHS gives 1837 as the establishment year and 1838 as the tower year; LighthouseFriends says the light was activated in March 1838. The NRHP's level-of-significance paragraph says 'Dating from 1827', which is not supported by its own chronology (probably an error). 2) Cost: NRHP 'built for $4500' against Congress's $5,000 in LighthouseFriends (also the Wikipedia lead, not cited). 3) Lens: LighthouseFriends has a fifth-order Fresnel lens in 1856; USLHS gives the original lens installed in 1888; the NRHP form describes the 1981 optic only. 4) Oil house: NRHP says stone, 1837 (text letter-spaced in the OCR, quoted only where clean); LighthouseFriends says brick, 1907. 5) Keeper's house move: NRHP chronology 1920; NRHP site description 1930; LighthouseFriends 1923 (the automation year). 6) The 1923 Bulletin entry is garbled in the OCR ('oil to engine and compressor, which have been acetylene, fixed to flashing'); only the index's 'change in illuminant' and the station name are quoted. 7) Hannah Braley (1846-1849) is a roster line only; the sources read do not say how she came to the post. 8) Larnet Hall: roster 1849 against LighthouseFriends 1848. 9) Russell B. Eastman: roster 1914-1923 here and 1925-1930 at Marblehead, both under the same archive person slug; no source read connects the two Marblehead and Ned's Point stints by name beyond the archive. LighthouseFriends places him as assistant keeper at Wing's Neck from 1923; the Wings Neck end year is not given, so no other_stations entry is made (data/stations/ma/us-ma-wings-neck.json exists). 10) The 1937 sale story is LighthouseFriends's account of a Pittsburgh Press (1 June 1937) and Sandusky Register (22 May 1937) report; neither newspaper was read here. 11) No Chronicling America search was run for Ned's Point. The Carpender 1838 report is quoted as LighthouseFriends prints it; the report itself was not read. 12) Today: the 2026 Friends schedule (Sippican, 1 June 2026) ran to 1 October 2026; the Friends' own site was not read. The tower is climbable only on tours; the keeper's wife and oil-hauling passages are LighthouseFriends's general account of the station and are attributed to it. Fact-check 2026-10-22: the 2026 tour notice (Sippican, 1 June 2026) names no Friends group and no tour leader by name; the story no longer attributes the tours to the Friends. The keeper named in the notice is a current keeper and is not named in the story. The 1918-1923 Bulletin index entry ('change in illuminant') is quoted; the 1923 Bulletin's Ned Point entry is OCR-garbled, so the story says only that the entry exists. The roster has eleven stints for ten people (Larnet Hall, Jr. has two). The 1981 form gives the reflectors as 13 1/3 inches; LighthouseFriends, quoting Carpender's 1838 report, as 13 1/2: both are stated. LighthouseFriends lists two 1937 newspapers in its references; the newspapers themselves were not read, and the story attributes the 1937 account to LighthouseFriends.
